<Note>If the user includes stop code in the Transactional SMS, then it will be switched to Marketing SMS automatically and it will be interpreted as a Marketing SMS. To send Transactional SMS as Transactional, it is important not to use stop code.
Note: For adding a stop code, client has to add reply STOP to [STOP_CODE] and the [STOP_CODE] will be replaced with the number.</Note>

items.docs: Retrieve an aggregated report of your transactional SMS activity over a specified time period, including counts for requests, delivered, hard bounces, soft bounces, blocked, unsubscribed, replied, accepted, rejected, and skipped messages. Filter by date range using `startDate` and `endDate` (both required together, YYYY-MM-DD format) or by a number of past `days` (not compatible with date range). Filter by date range using `startDate` and `endDate` (both required together, YYYY-MM-DD format), by a number of past `days` (not compatible with date range), or by `tag`. params.name: phoneNumber
params.description: Filter the report for a specific phone number

params.name: event
params.description: Filter the report for specific events

params.name: tags
params.description: Filter the report for specific tags passed as a serialized urlencoded array

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort the results in the ascending/descending order of record creation. Default order is **descending** if `sort` is not passed

items.docs: Retrieve a paginated list of individual SMS event records (unaggregated), including event type, phone number, message ID, timestamp, tag, and reason or reply content where applicable. Results default to 50 per page (max 100) and are sorted in descending order unless overridden. Filter by date range (`startDate`/`endDate`), past `days` (not compatible with date range), specific `event` type (e.g. delivered, bounces, replies), `phoneNumber`, or `tags`.
